summary: The order-submit failures are caused by degradation of the external exchange partner api.exchange-partner.example, not by the order-service v2.15.2 release (H2, confidence 0.75, high). Starting 11:01:25Z, exchange-gateway's outbound calls to that host began failing with 5s connect timeouts and application-layer 503s carrying the partner's own request id, pushing exchange-gateway's error rate to ~44% and p99 to ~4.8s; order-service, one hop downstream, shows ~30% submits failing with the identical error 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' and a pure downstream-wait latency profile with flat local CPU. The reporter's suspicion — the v2.15.2 release — is decisively rebutted: the rate was already at full ~30% magnitude before the 11:16Z rollback, was flat across the rollback second, and is still ~30-31% at 12:59Z, 1h43m later. Alternatives H3 (pricing-engine TTL change) and H4 (ledger-db/kafka shared-infra) are tested and contradicted by clean multi-metric evidence and cannot produce an exchange-gateway-scoped error signature. The remaining uncertainty is internal to H2 (partner-side outage vs. a DNS/egress/NAT/TLS path fault between exchange-gateway and the partner), which does not change the ranking or the remediation.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner degradation (api.exchange-partner.example) timing out exchange-gateway, propagating to order-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange API behind exchange-gateway stopped responding/timed out (connect timeouts after 5s, then application-layer 503s with the partner's own request id) starting 11:01:25Z. exchange-gateway's placeOrder/quoteSnapshot calls exceed the 5s timeout and a circuit breaker opens; this surfaces to order-service as 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)', giving ~30% order submit failures. order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) is coincidental: all order-service errors are the identical downstream signature, its local CPU is flat, and the failure rate is unchanged across the 11:16Z rollback.

causal_chain.claim: api.exchange-partner.example begins failing exchange-gateway's upstream calls: 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example' (op=placeOrder/quoteSnapshot) first_seen 11:01:25Z, plus application-layer 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' with x-partner-request-id first_seen 11:02:20Z
Circuit breaker for exchange-api opens at 11:03:26Z (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)

exchange-gateway error_rate ~0.2% -> ~44% and p99 130ms -> 4811ms in the same 11:00Z bucket, with flat request_rate ~265-280 req/s (not traffic-driven) and flat cpu_pct (~30%) / memory_pct (~44%) — no local saturation
order-service's placeOrder calls to exchange-gateway fail with 504 Gateway Timeout (349/350 errors identical); its p99 jumps to 4648.8ms while local CPU stays ~40% (pure downstream-wait)
order-service error_rate reaches ~30% and api-gateway propagates a smaller ~6% failure upstream; the partner-side error surface (connect timeouts + 503s) persists continuously to latest data 12:58Z

assumptions: The origin is the partner service/network itself rather than a DNS/egress/NAT/cert path fault between exchange-gateway and api.exchange-partner.example — no DNS/egress-change source and no partner telemetry exist (F4); the application-layer 503s carrying x-partner-request-id (F35) lean toward a real partner-side error surface but do not fully exclude a path fault.
Live traffic to the exchange was succeeding normally before 11:01Z (no pre-onset partner success metric retrieved).

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 regression (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The idempotency-key code release dep-5333 introduced a fault in order-service's submit path causing ~30% of submits to fail with 504s.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5333 (order-service v2.15.2, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit') deployed 10:48Z
New idempotency/retry-safe submit code path causes submits to stall or error
Failures surface as 504 Gateway Timeout on order submit

assumptions: order-service error text originates in order-service code rather than being a downstream failure it merely reports
the deploy precedes the onset (onset-vs-deploy ordering not proven from telemetry)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Every order-service error (349/350) is the identical downstream signature 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' (F8), and order-service's own CPU stayed flat ~40% with a pure downstream-wait latency profile (F9). The identical onset appears one hop further out at exchange-gateway (F10) with error text naming the external host (F11) before order-service logged anything (F12). Decisively, the 11:16Z rollback (F1) produced no recovery: the rate is flat across the rollback second (F21) and held ~30-31% through 12:45Z (F20/F22) and to 12:59Z (F23), and exchange-gateway's resources were flat (F31/F32) — incompatible with the release being the cause.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Pricing-engine cache TTL config change (5s -> 4s) degrading the quote path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only fleet-wide config change in the window (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20Z) caused pricing-engine to misbehave, and order-service 504s are timeouts waiting on pricing-engine/market-data.

causal_chain.claim: config-bot shortens pricing-engine cache TTL 5s -> 4s at 09:20Z
Reduced cache hit rate increases pricing-engine latency / downstream load
order-service submit calls pricing-engine and times out with 504

assumptions: the TTL change produces a delayed impact ~100 minutes later
order-service's failing dependency is pricing-engine despite the log text naming exchange-gateway
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine shows zero degradation: error_rate flat ~0.18-0.23% through 12:45Z and no WARN+ logs in 10:30-12:00Z (F16). The error signature names exchange-gateway, not pricing-engine (F8), and exchange-gateway's error text explicitly names the external host (F11).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared-infra / neighbour fault (ledger-db or kafka) independent of the release
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared component in order-service's neighbourhood (shared postgres ledger-db or shared kafka) degraded around 11:00Z, causing order-service submit timeouts and 504s independent of v2.15.2.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db / kafka is shared between order-service and portfolio/payment/settlement services
Shared component degrades around 11:00Z (IOPS throttling, connection exhaustion, broker issue)
order-service writes/swaps on the shared DB or produces to kafka and blocks
order-service error_rate rises to ~30% with 504s on submit

assumptions: a shared-infra fault exists that left no trace in the queried ledger-db metrics but would still produce an exchange-gateway-scoped error message
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: ledger-db is demonstrably healthy across the onset: slow_queries flat ~0.9-1.2/min (F13), connections_active flat ~61-63 (F14), only a benign 38ms NTP clock-drift WARN with no lock/slow-query warnings (F15). The failure is scoped to the external exchange call (F11) and precedes order-service errors (F12), which shared-infra cannot explain.

facts.statement: exchange-gateway's errors are upstream-call failures explicitly naming the external host: 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example' (op=placeOrder 163x, op=quoteSnapshot 146x, first_seen 11:01:25Z) and 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' (161x, first_seen 11:02:20Z); a circuit breaker opened for exchange-api at 11:03:26Z with failure ratio 0.47.

exchange-gateway showed the same onset as order-service and higher magnitude: error_rate rose from ~0.2% through 10:45Z to avg 40.44 / max 45.46 in the 11:00Z bucket (~44% sustained), with latency_p99_ms going from ~130ms to 4811ms avg in the same bucket.
Every order-service ERROR in the window (349 of 350 matched records) is the identical signature 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'; first occurrence 11:02:45Z.

order-service's own resources were stable across the onset: cpu_pct held ~39-42% in every 15-minute bucket from 07:00Z through 12:45Z (11:00Z avg 40.08), while latency_p99_ms jumped from flat ~148-154ms to 4648.8ms at 11:00Z — a downstream-wait signature, not local saturation.

exchange-gateway cpu_pct (min 26.73%, max 32.52%, mean 29.88%) and memory_pct (min 39.41%, max 48.55%, mean 44.11%) were flat across 10:30-12:59Z with no rise at or after onset, i.e. no local resource saturation.

order-service error_rate was flat at ~0.2% through the 10:45Z bucket, then jumped to avg 26.73 / max 33.2 in the 11:00Z bucket and stayed ~30-31% through 12:45Z; a 540s-bucket zoom puts onset in the 10:58Z bucket.

Pre-rollback, order-service error_rate was already at full magnitude: it jumped to ~30% within ~2 minutes (11:02Z 31.43, then 30.91, 29.95, 30.69, 30.21, 31.85, 31.66) well BEFORE the 11:16Z rollback.

There is no recovery at the rollback: 23 of 23 two-minute buckets in 11:15-12:00Z are elevated (min 28.43, max 33.32, mean 31.05), and a 60s zoom straddling the rollback second shows 11:15Z avg 32.87, 11:16Z 31.45, 11:17Z 31.73, 11:18Z 30.37 — flat, no recovery step.

The elevated rate persisted through 12:00-12:45Z (mean 31.05, range 28.38-35.57, no downward trend) and was still ~30-31% at latest data (12:57Z avg 31.49; 12:59Z avg 30.39), 1h43m after the rollback.
order-service request_rate was flat ~226-237 req/s across the whole period, so the ~30% is a fixed fraction of an unchanged workload, not a load surge.

In the fleet-wide change inventory for 06:00-12:59Z there was exactly ONE deployment: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) at 10:48:00Z, status rolled_back with rolled_back_at 11:16:00Z; and exactly ONE config change fleet-wide: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20:00Z.
pricing-engine shows no degradation: error_rate flat ~0.18-0.23% in every 15-minute bucket from 09:00Z through 12:45Z, and zero WARN+ records in 10:30-12:00Z.

ledger-db was healthy across the onset on multiple metrics: slow_queries_per_min flat ~0.9-1.2/min from 09:00Z to 12:45Z, connections_active flat ~61-63, and only a single benign 'clock drift 38ms' NTP WARN at 11:26:22Z with no errors, lock or slow-query warnings.

api-gateway (the only caller of order-service) shows the same 11:00Z onset but at ~6.1% sustained, a smaller magnitude than order-service's ~30%, consistent with it merely propagating downstream order-submit failures rather than originating them.

The partner failure path is not a transient blip: exchange-gateway connect-timeout errors to api.exchange-partner.example run continuously from 11:01:25Z to 12:58:30Z (309 ERROR records), and application-layer 503s with x-partner-request-id run from 11:02:20Z to 12:58:32Z (161 records), with steady per-bucket counts (~2-3 errors/min) rather than decaying to zero.

exchange-gateway is called by two independent in-fleet callers (order-service and market-data-service), and the external endpoint exchange-api is reachable solely via exchange-gateway; no deployment or config change was recorded for exchange-gateway or market-data-service in the window.

Historical precedent matches the current symptom set: HIST-103 (2025-10-21, 'Order failures during exchange partner outage', services order-service + exchange-gateway, symptoms '504 on order submit','upstream timeouts') was an external exchange API outage on the partner side.
order-service's dependency map shows it calls ledger-db, pricing-engine, exchange-gateway and kafka; exchange-gateway depends on external exchange-api which has no telemetry.

assumptions: The ultimate origin is the partner service/network itself rather than a DNS/egress/NAT/certificate path fault between exchange-gateway and api.exchange-partner.example — no DNS/egress-change source exists and no partner telemetry exists (F4); the application-layer 503s carrying x-partner-request-id lean toward a real partner-side error surface but do not fully exclude a path fault.
Live traffic to the exchange was succeeding normally before 11:01Z; no pre-onset partner success metric was retrieved.

The rollback of dep-5333 actually executed at 11:16:00Z as recorded in the deployment record (F1); an explicit restart-count step at that timestamp was not checked, though the error_rate shows no marker there regardless.

The 11:16Z rollback did not fix the incident because the cause lies outside order-service, rather than because the rollback itself was incomplete; no per-pod rollout timing for dep-5333 was available.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) exchange-gateway's request_rate was flat at ~265-280 req/s across the entire window including after 11:00Z, so its failure is not traffic-driven.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The exchange-gateway upstream failure starts at 11:01:25Z, i.e. order-service's reported failures (first log 11:02:45Z) are consequent to the gateway's upstream calls failing, consistent with a fast 5s timeout propagating to 504s.

timeline.event: Baseline check: no deployments and no config changes in the prior 24h before onset (get_deployments count 0, get_config_changes count 0).
Only fleet-wide config change in the window: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds changed 5 -> 4 by config-bot ('Shorter quote cache TTL').
Last clean bucket: order-service error_rate flat ~0.2% and p99 ~148-154ms; exchange-gateway error_rate ~0.2% and p99 ~130ms.
The only deployment in the window: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) by a.khan, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit'.
First exchange-gateway upstream failure to api.exchange-partner.example: 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms' (earliest error on the whole chain).
Partner-side application-layer errors appear: 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' carrying x-partner-request-id.
First order-service ERROR: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' — one hop and ~80 seconds after the gateway's upstream break.
Circuit breaker opens for exchange-api at exchange-gateway (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s).
Incident INC-003 reported (SEV-1): order submit failure rate ~30%, 504s on order submit; on-call begins rolling back v2.15.2.
60s zoom straddling the rollback shows the rate already flat at ~30%: 11:15Z 32.87, 11:16Z 31.45, 11:17Z 31.73, 11:18Z 30.37.
dep-5333 marked rolled_back — no recovery in error rate at or after this instant.
Only ledger-db WARN in the window: benign 'clock drift 38ms detected, resyncing with NTP' — no lock/slow-query warnings around the onset.
12:00-12:45Z remains elevated: mean 31.05%, range 28.38-35.57, no downward trend across 30 buckets.

Latest exchange-gateway upstream failure record still shows 'connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=quoteSnapshot'; partner 503 with x-partner-request-id last seen 12:58:32Z.
Incident unresolved at latest data: order-service error_rate still ~30-31% (12:57Z avg 31.49; 12:59Z avg 30.39), 1h43m after the rollback.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating the rollback as the fix and re-announce the incident as external-dependency-driven: confirm the rollback of dep-5333 is complete/stable, then freeze further order-service changes — the rate was already at full ~30% magnitude before the 11:16Z rollback and is flat across it (F19, F20, F21), and is still ~30-31% at 12:59Z (F23), so the rollback cannot resolve the incident.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 (release regression) is decisively rebutted by the unchanged rate across the rollback boundary; diverting effort to further rollback/redeploy work delays the real mitigation.

recommended_actions.action: Mitigate the exchange-gateway upstream path: raise or disable the 5s upstream connect timeout and relax/open the circuit breaker for exchange-api so calls degrade instead of hard-failing, and apply fail-fast/degraded-mode handling to exchange-dependent order submit paths in order-service (queue/retry with backoff rather than returning 504).
recommended_actions.rationale: The 5s connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example is the immediate mechanism converting partner slowness into ~44% exchange-gateway errors and ~30% order-submit 504s; the breaker is already open (failure ratio 0.47).

recommended_actions.action: Escalate to the exchange partner via the vendor relationship and open a partner ticket with timestamps and the captured x-partner-request-id values (first 11:02:20Z, latest 12:58:32Z), asking for their status for 11:01Z onward.
recommended_actions.rationale: The partner is returning its own application-layer 503s continuously, which is a partner-side error surface the vendor must answer for; this is the fastest path to recovery if the fault is truly partner-side.

recommended_actions.action: Run the discriminating check between partner-side outage and an egress-path fault on our side: query market-data-service error_rate/latency_p99 around 11:00-11:05Z (the second, independent caller of exchange-gateway), and check exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate/restarts plus DNS/egress/NAT/TLS-cert change feeds for the exchange-gateway -> api.exchange-partner.example path.
recommended_actions.rationale: If market-data-service also broke at ~11:01Z, the fault is partner-side rather than exchange-gateway-local; if only order-service traffic is affected, an egress-path fault is more likely. This resolves the one remaining open element inside H2 and determines who owns the fix.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery against the same signal that defined the fault: verify exchange-gateway's connect-timeout/503 counts to api.exchange-partner.example return to zero and order-service error_rate returns to ~0.2% (its flat pre-onset baseline), and only then close the incident.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure is continuous rather than decaying (309 timeout records and 161 partner 503s through 12:58Z), so closure must be tied to the upstream signature disappearing, not to time elapsed.

recommended_actions.action: Add upstream-partner health to alerting and add an order-submit degradation path that does not convert partner slowness into user-visible 504s (explicit timeout budget per downstream hop, request hedging or queue-and-confirm for exchange-dependent submits).
recommended_actions.rationale: This incident reproduced a known historical pattern (HIST-103: external exchange API outage producing 504s on order submit), so recurrence prevention should target blast-radius reduction at the exchange-gateway boundary.

recommended_actions.action: Tighten release-vs-incident discrimination in the on-call runbook: before rolling back a same-day deploy, check whether the error signature is entirely a downstream dependency message and whether the rate is flat across the deploy/rollback boundary — and align the v2.15.2 deploy timestamp (only 10:48Z is recorded) against a second-level onset series so future incidents do not spend ~40 minutes on a coincidental release.
recommended_actions.rationale: The same-day dep-5333 deploy (10:48Z) was coincidental with the 11:01Z partner onset, and ~100 minutes of rollback effort were spent on it despite a pure downstream-wait signature and flat local CPU.

data_gaps: No telemetry exists for the external exchange endpoint api.exchange-partner.example (has_telemetry: false, out of fleet scope), so the ultimate origin — partner-side service outage vs. a network/DNS/egress/NAT/TLS path fault between exchange-gateway and the partner — cannot be confirmed from internal data. This bounds H2's confidence at 0.75.

market-data-service error_rate/latency metrics around the 11:00Z onset were never retrieved (budget exhausted), so the decisive test for whether the second independent caller of exchange-gateway also broke — which would mark the fault as partner-side rather than gateway-local — is unanswered (F30).

exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate and restart counts were not retrieved (query budget exhausted), so the upstream failure rate is only derivable from log counts (309 timeout records; ~2-3/min) and it is unverified whether exchange-gateway restarted, which could otherwise explain a resource change.

No DNS / egress-firewall / NAT / TLS-certificate change source was available or queried for the exchange-gateway -> partner path; only deployment and config inventories were checked (both returned zero entries). An infrastructure-layer change on the egress path would not appear in those feeds.

order-service v2.15.2's exact deploy time is not present in retrieved data (only the 10:48Z record from the deployment inventory), and no per-pod rollout timing/canary percentage was available, so the onset-vs-deploy ordering cannot be strictly proven from telemetry — only that onset (11:01Z) precedes the rollback (11:16Z).

No sub-minute comparison of api-gateway vs. exchange-gateway vs. order-service onset buckets was obtained; the ordering relies on log timestamps (exchange-gateway first error 11:01:25Z) rather than metric buckets, which all straddle the onset at 11:00Z.

Kafka/queue metrics and metrics+logs for the shared-infra neighbours portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service were not queried, so a host-level shared-infra contribution reaching order-service via neighbours cannot be fully excluded (though ledger-db itself is clean on multiple metrics).
The order-service log query was truncated (40 of 350 records returned), so additional distinct error signatures between 11:02 and 12:58 could exist, though none appeared in top_patterns.

No explicit restart-count step for order-service at 11:16Z was checked; the rollback time is taken from the deployment record, not re-derived. This does not affect the exoneration conclusion, since the error rate shows no marker at that timestamp.
Tool reliability: one query (query_metrics ledger-db latency_p99_ms) failed with not_found, and two calls returned budget_exhausted, limiting coverage of exchange-gateway and neighbouring services.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Market-data-service (the second, independent caller of exchange-gateway) showing NO error/latency degradation at ~11:01Z while only order-service traffic fails — that would point to an exchange-gateway-local fault or an order-service-specific path/credential issue rather than a partner-wide outage.

Discovery of a DNS record, firewall/egress or NAT rule, or TLS certificate change on the exchange-gateway -> api.exchange-partner.example path at ~11:00Z, which would move the origin from the partner to our egress path.

Partner confirmation that their service was healthy at 11:01Z onward despite the 503s, or evidence that the 503s carrying x-partner-request-id are generated by an intermediary, which would invalidate the partner-side error-surface reading.

Evidence that order-service's error rate recovered or dropped at any point after the 11:16Z rollback (it did not through 12:59Z) — a genuine recovery step at the rollback boundary would reopen H1 (v2.15.2 regression).

A distinct order-service error signature (not the downstream 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504') appearing on the submit path, or a targeted code-level read showing dep-5333's idempotency-key change can itself produce submit failures, which would re-raise H1.
New degradation evidence for pricing-engine (error_rate or WARN+ logs) or for ledger-db/kafka on metrics not yet queried (slow queries, connections, kafka produce path), which would reopen H3 or H4.

These are leads, not evidence about the current incident.

Through the latest data at 12:59Z the rate is still ~30-31%: 12:57Z avg 31.49 (max 32.44), 12:59Z avg 30.39 — 1h43m after the rollback the incident is unresolved.

order-service request_rate was flat ~226-237 req/s across the whole period (10:30Z-12:59Z, 12 buckets), so the ~30% is a fixed fraction of an unchanged workload, not a load surge masking a recovering error count.

exchange-gateway has TWO independent in-fleet callers: order-service -> exchange-gateway (http) AND market-data-service -> exchange-gateway (http), plus exchange-gateway -> exchange-api (external). market-data-service is not in the order-service dependency chain shown by F4 (order-service -> pricing-engine -> market-data-service), so a market-data-service failure could not be caused by order-service's v2.15.2 deploy.

The only external endpoint node is 'exchange-api' (type external, owner vendor, has_telemetry false) reachable solely via exchange-gateway -> exchange-api; no other service has an edge to the partner host, so all places that 'call api.exchange-partner.example' do so through exchange-gateway (order-service and market-data-service are the callers of exchange-gateway).

No deployment was recorded for exchange-gateway or market-data-service in the 24h+ window 2026-03-16T00:00Z-2026-03-17T13:00Z: get_deployments for exchange-gateway returned count 0, and the fleet-wide 06:00-12:59Z inventory still contains exactly one deployment (dep-5333 order-service v2.15.2).

No config change was recorded for exchange-gateway (count 0 for 2026-03-16T00:00Z-2026-03-17T13:00Z) or market-data-service (count 0 for 06:00-12:59Z); the fleet-wide config inventory still holds only pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (cfg-2290) at 09:20Z.

Historical precedent matches the current symptom set closely: HIST-103 (2025-10-21, 'Order failures during exchange partner outage', services order-service + exchange-gateway, symptoms '504 on order submit','upstream timeouts') was an 'External exchange API outage on the partner side' (dependency_failure) — a lead only, not evidence about the current incident.

findings.statement: Because market-data-service reaches exchange-gateway independently of order-service and of order-service's v2.15.2 deploy, a market-data-service error/latency jump at ~11:01Z would mark the break as partner-side rather than exchange-gateway-local; I could not retrieve those metrics within budget, so the discrimination between H2 (partner outage) and an exchange-gateway-side DNS/egress fault is left unresolved by this task.

exchange-gateway cpu_pct was flat across the whole 10:30-12:59Z window, including before and after the 11:00Z onset: min 26.73%, max 32.52%, mean 29.88% over 150 points with missing_points 0; the 10:58Z bucket (just before onset) avg 29.93 / max 31.52, the 11:05Z bucket avg 30.15 / max 32.52, and the latest 12:57Z bucket avg 30.49 / max 31.63. No CPU rise at or after onset.

exchange-gateway memory_pct was likewise flat across 10:30-12:59Z: min 39.41%, max 48.55%, mean 44.11%, missing_points 0; 10:58Z avg 44.5 / max 47.07, 11:05Z avg 44.75 / max 48.01, and latest 12:57Z avg 43.08 / max 44.38. No memory pressure or growth coinciding with the onset, i.e. no local resource saturation.

The api.exchange-partner.example upstream failure path is still broken at latest data, not a transient blip: exchange-gateway connect-timeout errors to that host run continuously from first_match 11:01:25Z to last_match 12:58:30Z (309 ERROR records in 10:30-12:59Z), with the most recent entry '2026-03-17T12:58:30Z ... upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=quoteSnapshot'. Bucket-level counts confirm continuity: 11:00-11:15Z = 40 matched, 12:00-12:15Z = 31 matched (first 12:00:32Z), 12:45-12:59Z = 39 matched (first 12:45:33Z).

The same two upstream failure signatures persist across the requested buckets with matching per-bucket counts: 11:00-11:15Z showed 23x op=placeOrder (first_seen 11:01:25Z) and 17x op=quoteSnapshot (first_seen 11:01:43Z); 12:00-12:15Z 17x placeOrder / 14x quoteSnapshot; 12:45-12:59Z 20x quoteSnapshot / 19x placeOrder. So the failure rate to the partner is steady (~2-3 errors/min) rather than decaying to zero.

The partner is also returning application-layer 503s the whole time: 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable (x-partner-request-id=...)' matched 161 ERROR records, first_match 11:02:20Z and last_match 2026-03-17T12:58:32Z, e.g. 12:58:32Z 'x-partner-request-id=b62798d4'. This is a real partner-side error surface (not just a network connect timeout) and it is still present at latest data.
